title: A novel compound PT‐262 inhibits Oct4 and Nanog on the survivin blockage and apoptosis induction in human lung cancer
abstract: PT‐262 (7‐chloro‐6‐piperidin‐1‐yl‐quinoline‐5, 8‐dione) is a novel synthetic compound, which derived from 6, 7‐dichloro‐quinoline‐5, 8‐diones that shows anticancer activities. However, the inhibition of cancer stem cells (CSC) and tumor growth in lung cancer by PT‐262 is still unclear. Here, we show that PT‐262 effectively inhibits the cancer stem proteins of Oct4 and Nanog, which are transcription factors in regulating CSC malignancy. Overexpressing Oct and Nanog in A549 lung cancer cells induced CSC‐like cell line, which we called A549‐ON, displayed drug resistance to chemotherapeutics. Interestingly, PT‐262 elicited higher cell death in the A549‐ON than the parental A549 cells. PT‐262 inhibited the protein expression of Oct4 and Nanog associated with survivin suppression and apoptotic induction. Moreover, A549‐ON cells expressed higher survivin protein levels. Transfection of Oct4 vector in A549 cells increased survivin protein expression. Besides, PT‐262 inhibited the anchorage‐independent ability and the xenografted lung tumor growth of SCID mice. Together, these results demonstrate that PT‐262 has ability to inhibit CSC malignancy and tumorigenesis in lung cancer.
